chosen_layout.caption: Sepulchre’s postdoctoral work with Petar Kokotović opens a selected MGP route through control, physics, chemistry and medicine. Older links are historical teaching or influence records, with uncertainty shown.
chosen_layout.compact_names_recent_to_older: Rodolphe Sepulchre ← Petar Kokotović ← Alexander Feldbaum ← Aleksandr Andronov ← Leonid Mandelstam ← Karl Ferdinand Braun ← Georg Hermann Quincke ← Heinrich Gustav Magnus ← Eilhard Mitscherlich ← Friedrich Stromeyer ← Johann Friedrich Gmelin ← Philipp Friedrich Gmelin ← Burchard David Mauchart ← Elias Rudolph Camerarius Jr. ← Elias Rudolph Camerarius Sr. ← Georg Balthasar Metzger ← Johann Jakob von Brunn ← Johannes Nicolaus Stupanus ← Theodor Zwinger ← Bassiano Landi ← Giovanni Battista della Monte ← Niccolò Leoniceno ← Ognibene Bonisoli da Lonigo ← Vittorino da Feltre ← Guarino da Verona ← Manuel Chrysoloras ← Demetrios Kydones ← Nilos Kabasilas ← Gregory Palamas ← Theodore Metochites ← Manuel Bryennios ← Gregory Chioniades ← Shams al-Dīn al-Bukhārī ← Nasir al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī ← Kamal al-Din Ibn Yunus ← Sharaf al-Din al-Masudi al-Marwazi ← Omar Khayyam ← Bahmanyār ibn al-Marzubān ← Avicenna · Ibn Sina

limitations: The 39-person main route is complete as a sequence of directly inspected MGP Advisor links plus the separately sourced Sepulchre–Kokotović postdoctoral link. It is not a continuous independently proven doctoral pedigree to Avicenna.

Rodolphe’s postdoctoral mentorship is with Petar Kokotović. Mrdjan Janković was another postdoctoral researcher and coauthor in the same project, not evidence of an additional postdoctoral supervisor.

Kokotović’s MGP entry lists both Yakov Tsypkin and Alexander Feldbaum. His IEEE oral history confirms he began with Feldbaum and moved to Tsypkin after Feldbaum suffered a stroke. The selected older route uses Feldbaum, while a short optional Tsypkin–Aizerman branch rejoins Andronov.
Tsypkin’s 1945 Ph.D. adviser is unknown. Aizerman belongs to his 1948 D.Sc. record. Andronov is explicitly an opponent in Tsypkin’s entry and is not represented as his direct adviser in this tree.

Metzger’s selected link to von Brunn belongs to his medical doctorate (Basel 1650), not his Jena Magister record. Zwinger’s selected link to Landi belongs to his Padua medical doctorate (1559), not his earlier degree with Ramus.

Mitscherlich’s Stromeyer link is displayed as MGP-recorded academic mentorship; the MGP entry associates an 1814 literary degree and Persian-history dissertation with this adviser, which has not been independently validated as doctoral supervision.

Leoniceno’s Bonisoli link follows his earlier school/B.A. record, not his medical doctorate. From there toward Avicenna use dashed historical links, without generic Ph.D. labels or invented degree dates.
The Khayyam–Bahmanyār connection is explicitly qualified as possible in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Preserve that uncertainty even when the intermediate scholars are collapsed.

The Byzantine and Persian teacher/influence links are verified as MGP records but not all independently verified from specialist historical scholarship. Do not call the whole route a proven chain of personal supervision.
This is a selected branch, not the complete many-parent MGP network. MGP depends substantially on contributed data; original diplomas and manuscripts were not inspected for every entry.

additional_support.claim: Primary, jointly signed preface, dated Santa Barbara August 1996, verifies the UCSB postdoctoral relationship.
Kokotović’s first-person account confirms Feldbaum and Tsypkin mentorship and his 1965 candidate degree. Paraphrase rather than reproducing passages.
Scholarly reference qualifies the Bahmanyār connection as possible and rejects direct study with Avicenna.

Avicenna was a philosopher and physician; Latin translations of his Canon underpinned European medical instruction into the seventeenth century. This is intellectual context, not an added supervisor edge.
Specialist study describes letters between Avicenna and his disciple Bahmanyār, supporting their historical association.
Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers entry by Katherine Haramundanis identifies Chioniades as a physician. Supports the subtitle; no new edge inferred.
MGP explains its substantial reliance on contributed records.

alternative_conservative_layout.instruction: If the site requires only independently corroborated personal supervision, show the sourced modern/medical segment, insert a visible historical gap, and show Avicenna separately as a medicine-and-philosophy root with the SEP contextual citation. Do not draw a solid uninterrupted connection to him.
